answer: New agents enter probation and can only receive small payments until established participants stake funds behind them. If a newcomer defaults or colludes in a detected fraud, its backers lose part of their stake, so endorsements carry real liability rather than being free accounts. A sybil attacker must recruit independent backers or lock up capital across identities, raising the cost of faking trust; names like shale, quartz, and basalt can label separate stake pools without changing the rule.
